title: I missed the deep co-op tower defense of Warcraft 3's YouTD, so I spent a year building my own. Defense of Solaris is now in open beta (free, in the browser)
author: Wulffman96
selftext:
Last September I started building the game I thought of for a long time creating.

I grew up on Warcraft 3 tower defense maps, a favourite of mine was YouTD, where towers had items, levels and passives and felt more like ARPG builds than turrets. Most tower defense games I've played since are either fairly shallow mechanically or single-player. I wanted that deep, buildcrafting feeling with friends, and co-op that actually matters instead of just sharing a map.

Today Defense of Solaris enters open beta. It's free and of course in the ai gaming age runs in your browser.

What it is:

* Co-op for up to 12 players: hold your lane together, send items to teammates, and vote on where the Ritual goes next.
* ARPG-style builds: 26 towers across three factions, each with upgrade tiers, levels, passives and item slots. There are 100+ items, including legendaries that change how a tower works. One sets a tower's hit damage to 1 but multiplies its damage over time by 1.6.
* Roguelite meta-progression: Commanders with skill trees that grow across runs.
* Deck building: you bring a Legion Deck into every run, and it decides which towers you can build. Towers can also be sacrificed for an effect, like flipping a card.

It's a beta, so balance will move and there will be rough edges. I'd love to hear what feels good and what doesn't.

You can find some introductory videos on Youtube: [https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLAWvnDSbd\_Mc](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLAWvnDSbd_Mc)
